Rashi on Shabbat 90a:10:1.hebrew: מקק דסיפרי תכך דשיראי - כל אלו תולעין הן שבכל מין ומין, וחלוקין בשמותיהם — תכך, איילא, פה, הה:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:10:1.english: Mekek of scrolls, tekhakh of silk - All of these are worms that are in each and every species, and they differ in their names — tekhakh, ayla, pe, ha.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:10:2.english: All of them [are] a danger - To one who eats them.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:10:3.hebrew: קוצים יש בתאנים - היה תולעת יושב ונוקב בגרונו, ודומה שהוא קוץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:10:3.english: Are there thorns in figs? - A worm was sitting and puncturing his throat, and it seemed [to him] that it was a thorn.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:10:4.english: The pe killed this [one] - The pe killed this [one].

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:11:1.hebrew: רוכלין - מוכרי בשמים לקישוטי נשים, ויש להן קופות קטנות לצרורות בשמים:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:11:1.english: Merchants - Sellers of spices for women's adornments, and they have small baskets for bundles of spices.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:11:2.english: [He] is liable [for] only one sin-offering - Because all of it is one [act of] carrying out.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:11:3.hebrew: פחות מכגרוגרת - דאע"ג דכל האוכלין שיעורן כגרוגרת, הני, כיון דלזריעה קיימי, בפחות מכגרוגרת נמי מיחייב:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:11:3.english: Less than a dried fig's bulk - For although the measure [for liability] of all foods is a dried fig's bulk, [with regard to] these [garden seeds], since they are meant for sowing, one is liable even for less than a dried fig's bulk.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:1:1.hebrew: במיני מתיקה - עסקינן שכולן מיני מתיקת קדירה, אבל מין אחר אין מצטרף, ומתניתין לא מפליג:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:1:1.english: With sweet types - we are dealing [with a case] where all of them are types for sweetening a pot, but another type does not combine [with them], and our Mishnah does not distinguish [between them].

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:2:1.hebrew: דוגמא לאירא - מעט צמר שהוא כמין דוגמא שמראה הצבע לבע"ה: "כזה תחפוץ או כזה?", והוא כדי ליתן באירא של קנה של גרדי, ושיעורה מועט:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:2:1.english: A sample for the shuttle - [This is] a small amount of wool that is a sort of sample that the dyer shows to the patron: "Do you want [one] like this or like that?" And it is [only] enough to put in the shuttle of a weaver's reed, and its measure is small.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:2:2.hebrew: לשרות - ומתני' בשאינן שרויין, והבא לשרות אינו שורה פחות מכדי בגד קטן:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:2:2.english: To soak - And our Mishnah [refers to] when they are not soaked, and one who comes to soak [them] does not soak less than enough for a small garment.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:4:1.english: They added to them - Regarding the Sabbatical year.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:4:5.hebrew: שיש לו עיקר - שנשרש בארץ. ולפי דעתי, תורניסא דגרסינן במס' ע"ז דבר שאין לו שורש — הוא כמו זה, ולא כמו שמפרשין אותו פיונ"א:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:4:5.english: That has a root - [Meaning,] that takes root in the ground. And in my opinion, [the] tornisa that we read [about] in Tractate Avodah Zarah — something that has no root — is like this, and not as [those who] explain it [to be] peonia [peony].

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:5:1.hebrew: שלוף דוץ - לא איתפרש, אבל כך שמו:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:5:1.english: Shelof dotz - [Its meaning] was not explained, rather this is its name.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:5:2.english: With an iron skewer - An iron piercer [or borer; Old French: foredoire].

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:6:1.hebrew: פלפלת כל שהוא - ואינו פלפל שלנו, ובגמרא מפרש כל שהוא למאי חזי:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:6:1.english: Pepper, any amount - And it is not our pepper, and in the Gemara it explains what any amount is fit for.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:6:2.english: Kinds of spices, any amount - For a pleasant fragrance.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:6:3.hebrew: מיני מתכות כל שהוא - ראוי לדרבן קטן. שמצניעין אותו לרפואה, ל"ג:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:6:3.english: Kinds of metals, any amount - [It is] fit for a small goad. [The phrase] "that they store it away for healing" — we do not read [it in the text].

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:6:4.hebrew: מקק ספרים - אכילת תולעת אוכלת הספרים ומרקבן, ושמו מקק:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:6:4.english: Mekak of scrolls - [The] eating of a worm [that] eats the scrolls and causes them to rot, and its name is mekak.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:6:5.english: That they store them away to bury them - Because every sacred object requires burial.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:6:6.hebrew: מאומה - אלמא אחשביה קרא לאיסורא. והא דתנן (לעיל שבת דף עה.) כל שאינו כשר להצניע כו', ואוקימנא למעוטי עצי אשירה, דלא כר' יהודה:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:6:6.english: Anything [me’umah] - Thus we see that the verse accorded significance to a prohibited item. And as for that which we learned in a Mishnah (above, Shabbat 75a), “Whatever is not fit to store, etc.,” which we established as excluding wood of an asheirah — [that Mishnah is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:7:1.english: For tzilchata - Pain of half the head [i.e., a migraine].

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:7:2.hebrew: ריח רע - שמעשנין בהן חולין ותינוקות, כגון חלטית, להבריח מעליו מזיקין:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:7:2.english: A foul odor - [A substance] with which they fumigate sick people and infants, such as asafoetida, to drive away harmful spirits from them.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:7:3.hebrew: ארגמן - צבע שצובעין בו ארגמן, וטעמא לא איתפרש. ול"נ שגם הוא ראוי להריח:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:7:3.english: Purple dye - A dye with which one dyes purple, and the reason [for its measure] was not explained. And it seems to me that it too is fit for smelling.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:7:4.english: A virgin rose - One petal of a young rose.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:8:1.hebrew: מיני מתכות כל שהוא - מתני' היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:8:1.english: Kinds of metals, any amount - [This] is [from] the Mishnah.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:9:1.english: [It is incumbent] upon me [to donate] iron - for the upkeep of the Temple.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:9:2.hebrew: לכליא עורב - טבלאות של אמה היו עושין, והן חדין כסכין סביבותיהם, ומסמרין חדין בכולן, ומחפין בהן גגו של היכל למנוע את העורבים מלישב:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:9:2.english: For a raven impediment - They would make plates of a cubit [by a cubit], and they [were] sharp as a knife all around, and [had] sharp nails throughout them, and they would cover the roof of the Sanctuary with them to prevent the ravens from perching [there].

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:9:3.english: Than a ma'ah of silver - Copper worth a ma'ah of silver.

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:9:4.hebrew: צנורא - מזלג קטן [כעין] שטוין בו זהב. ולבדק הבית למאי חזי:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:9:4.english: Tzinora - A small fork [like that] with which they spin gold. And for Temple upkeep, for what is it fit?

Rashi on Shabbat 90a:9:5.hebrew: שמוחטין בו פתילות - ומנקבין ראשיהן לעדויי חושכן, מוקיי"ר:
Rashi on Shabbat 90a:9:5.english: With which they scrape wicks - And pierce their tips to remove their darkness [i.e., the charred part], mouchier [Old French: to snuff a wick].

Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:11:1.hebrew: המוציא קופת הרוכלין אע"פ שיש בה מינין הרבה אינו חייב אלא אחת - תימה, דמאי קמ"ל? פשיטא, דאפילו בהוציא וחזר והוציא אינו חייב אלא אחת, כמו בקצר וחזר וקצר — כ"ש בבת אחת! ואפילו רב יוסף דמחייב אליבא דר' אליעזר בקצר וחזר וקצר בפרק אמרו לו (יומא דף טו.), בהוצאה אחת פשיטא דפטור. ותירץ ר"ת דמיירי כגון שנודע לו על מין זה ונתכפר, וחזר ונודע לו על מין אחר — אפ"ה פטור, דהוי הכל כמו דבר אחד. ואע"ג דבפרק המצניע (לקמן שבת צג:) תניא: "ואם היה כלי צריך לו — חייב אף על הכלי", ומוקי לה רב אשי ששגג בזה ובזה, ונודע לו וחזר ונודע לו, ובפלוגתא דרבי יוחנן ור"ל — דוקא בכלי ואוכלים שבתוכו מחלקין ידיעות, אבל באוכלין שבתוך הכלי, אפילו כפרות אין מחלקות. ור"י מצא בירושלמי: "אילו הוציא והוציא, כלום הוא חייב אלא אחת? לא נצרכה אלא לר"א, שלא תאמר מינים הרבה יעשו כהעלמות הרבה ויהא חייב על כל אחת ואחת — קמ"ל." פי': דס"ד דמינים מחלקין, כדא"ר יהושע: "תמחויין מחלקין". ומיהו ה"ל להזכיר ר' יהושע:
Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:11:1.english: One who carries out a merchant's basket, even if there are many types in it, is obligated [to bring] only one [sin-offering] - [This is] astonishing: what is [the Mishnah] teaching us? It is obvious! For even if one carried out [one item] and then carried out [another item] again, he is obligated [to bring] only one [sin-offering], just as in [the case of] one who reaped and reaped again — all the more so [when carrying them out] all at once! And even Rav Yosef, who holds [one] liable [for each act] according to R. Eliezer in [the case of] one who reaped and reaped again in the chapter Amru Lo (Yoma 15a) — in a single act of carrying out, it is obvious that he is exempt [from multiple offerings]. And Rabbeinu Tam answered that [the Mishnah] is dealing with a case where it became known to him [that he sinned] regarding this type and he received atonement, and then it became known to him regarding another type — even so, he is exempt [from a second offering], for it is all like one thing. And even though in the chapter Hamatzni'a (below, Shabbat 93b) it is taught [in a Baraita]: "And if the vessel was needed by him, he is liable for the vessel as well," and Rav Ashi establishes it [as referring to a case] where he acted unwittingly regarding both this [the food] and that [the vessel], and it became known to him [regarding one] and then became known to him [regarding the other], and [it depends] on the dispute between R. Yochanan and Reish Lakish — [nevertheless,] specifically regarding a vessel and the foods inside it do instances of awareness divide [liability], whereas regarding [different types of] foods inside the vessel, even [separate] atonements do not divide [liability]. And R. Yitzchak found in the Jerusalem Talmud: "If he carried out [one item] and [then] carried out [another], would he be obligated [to bring] anything other than one [sin-offering]? [The Mishnah] is needed only according to R. Eliezer, lest you say that many types should be treated like many periods of unawareness and he would be liable for each and every one — [therefore, the Mishnah] teaches us [otherwise]." Explanation: [The reason one might have thought so is] that it might have entered your mind that [different] types divide [liability], as R. Yehoshua says: "Dishes divide [liability]." However, [the Jerusalem Talmud] should have mentioned R. Yehoshua [rather than R. Eliezer].

Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:1:1.hebrew: הואיל וראויין למתק הקדירה - "הואיל וממתיקין" הוה ליה למימר, כדפי' בסוף כלל גדול (שבת דף עו. ושם). וא"ת: היכי מיירי? אי בנותן טעם — אפילו שאר מינין נמי; ואי אין בהם נותן טעם — אפי' מיני מתיקה נמי לא! וי"ל: דאפילו ביש בהן נותן טעם שרי בשאר מינין, דנותן טעם לפגם הוא. ר"י:
Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:1:1.english: Since they are fit to sweeten the pot - [The Gemara] should have said "since they sweeten," as we explained at the end of [chapter] Kelal Gadol (Shabbat 76a and there). And if you ask: With what case are we dealing? If [it is a case] where [the spices] impart flavor, [then] even other species [should] also [join together and be prohibited]; and if they do not impart flavor, [then] even sweet types [should] not [be prohibited] either! And one can answer: Even when they impart flavor, it is permitted in the case of other species, because it is an imparting of flavor to the detriment [of the food]. R"I.

Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:3:1.hebrew: מי רגלים בן מ' יום - אין גירסא זו נכונה, דמשמע של קטן בן מ' יום; ובנדה פרק האשה (דף סב.) גבי ז' סממנין מעבירין, קתני כל הני דהכא, ומי רגלים, וקא בעי התם בגמרא: דילד או מזקן? ואית דגרסי: של מ' יום. ואין נראה, דהתם נמי תניא: ומי רגלים שהחמיצו, וכמה חימוצן? שלשה ימים. ונראה כספרים דגרסי: עד מ' יום, דמג' ימים עד מ' מעבירין אותם על הכתם, אבל תוך ג' ולאחר מ' אין מעבירין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:3:1.english: "Urine forty days old" - This reading is not correct, as it implies [the urine] of a child forty days old; and in Niddah, in the chapter [entitled] HaIshah (62a), regarding the seven substances [that] remove [stains], it teaches all these [materials mentioned] here, as well as urine, and the Gemara there asks: [Urine] of a child or of an elderly person? And there are those who read: "[urine] of forty days." But [this] does not seem [correct], for there too it is taught [in a baraita]: "And urine that has fermented; and how long is its fermentation? Three days." And [the reading] of the texts that read "up to forty days" appears [correct], for from three days until forty [days] one passes them over the stain [to remove it], whereas within three [days] or after forty [days] one does not pass [them]:

Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:3:2.hebrew: בורית זה החול - ואע"ג דבפ' המוציא (לעיל שבת פ:) יהיב בחול שיעורא אחרינא, "כדי ליתן על פי כף של סיד" — אומר רבינו מאיר דהתם מיירי בחול שנותנין בסיד, אבל הכא איירי בחול שמלבנין בו את הבגדים. ולספרים דגרסי הכא "בורית זה אהלא", אתי שפיר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:3:2.english: Borit — that is sand - And even though in the chapter [entitled] HaMotzi (above, Shabbat 80b), [the Mishnah] gives a different measure for sand — "enough to put on the opening of a lime trowel" — Rabbeinu Meir says that there it is referring to sand that is put into lime, whereas here it is referring to sand with which they whiten garments. And according to the texts that read here, "Borit — that is ahala," it works out well.

Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:4:1.hebrew: תרי גווני אהלא - ולעיל דלא שני תרי גווני חול (או לגירסא אחרת: תרי גוונא אהלא), משום דקים ליה דליכא בהו תרי גוונין. ויש ספרים דגרסי לעיל: "מאי בורית — אהלא", ולפי זה אתי שפיר, דה"ק: לעולם כדאמר מעיקרא דבורית זה אהלא, ותרי גווני אהלא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:4:1.english: Two types of aloe - And above, [the reason] that [the Gemara] did not answer "two types of sand" (or, according to another reading: "two types of aloe") is because it was certain that there are not two types of them. And there are texts that read above: "What is borit? Aloe," and according to this it works out well, for this is what [the Gemara] is saying: Actually, [it is] as it said originally, that borit is aloe, and [there are] two types of aloe.

Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:9:1.hebrew: מכליא עורב - בערוך בערך כל פי', דבמקדש ראשון מפני רוב קדושה שהיתה בו לא הוה צריך כליא עורב. וליתא, דבפ"ק דמועד קטן (דף ט.) מוכח בהדיא שהיה במקדש ראשון כליא עורב:
Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:9:1.english: [No less] than a raven impediment - In the Arukh, under the entry Kal, [he] explained that in the First Temple, because of the abundance of sanctity that was in it, a raven impediment was not needed. However, this is not so, for in the first chapter of Moed Katan (9a) it is explicitly proven that there was a raven impediment in the First Temple.

Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:9:2.hebrew: לא יפחות ממעה כסף - תימה לר"י, ד"לא יפחות מפרוטה" הוה ליה למימר, כי היכי דתניא בפרק בתרא דמנחות (דף קו:): "הרי עלי זהב — לא יפחות מדינר זהב, כסף — לא יפחות מדינר כסף":
Tosafot on Shabbat 90a:9:2.english: He shall not give less than a ma'ah of silver - This is astonishing to Rabbi Yitzchak, for [the baraita] should have said "he shall not give less than a perutah" [of copper], just as it is taught in the last chapter of Menachot (106b): "[One who says:] 'It is incumbent upon me [to donate] gold' — he shall not give less than a gold dinar; [if he says] 'silver' — he shall not give less than a silver dinar."
